ci_final_capstone_step1.title: Build the Product Catalog
ci_final_capstone_step1.prompt: Start the launch database with a `products` table. Use an integer primary id. Require a unique SKU, name, category, price, and status. New products should begin with a `draft` status when no status is supplied, while notes may remain empty. Inspect the stored product definition in `query.sql`.
ci_final_capstone_step1.hint: This first milestone establishes the complete product catalog rules before any rows are loaded.

help.concept: A launch schema should encode identity, required values, uniqueness, and defaults before data arrives.
help.hint_1: The SKU is a business identifier in addition to the table's primary id.
help.hint_2: The status has both a required-value rule and an initial default.

    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    sku TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    category TEXT NOT NULL,
    price REAL NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',
    notes TEXT
);

ci_final_capstone_step2.title: Add the Stock Event Ledger
ci_final_capstone_step2.prompt: Carry the product schema forward. Add `stock_events` with an integer primary id, a required product id, a required integer quantity change, and a required event type that defaults to `receipt`. Notes may remain empty. Connect each event's product id to the product table, then inspect both stored table definitions.
ci_final_capstone_step2.hint: Preserve the completed product table and add only the new event-ledger definition.

help.concept: The child table records stock history while the foreign key protects its relationship to products.
help.hint_1: Every event must belong to a valid product.
help.hint_2: The event type receives the receipt default.

help.concept: A production correction should combine the approved assignments with a narrow row condition.

practice-launch-review-mutations.title: Practice: Rehearse the Launch Review

In `operations.sql`, change product 2 so its price becomes `22.50` and its status becomes `active`, using its id as the safety boundary. Then remove the stock event whose note is `Placeholder`. In `query.sql`, verify product 2's final price and status and confirm that no placeholder event remains.
practice-launch-review-mutations.hint: Preserve the supplied schema and seed data. Add one scoped update and one scoped delete.

help.concept: A launch review combines precise mutations with final state verification.

help.hint_2: Only the event identified by the Placeholder note is approved for deletion.
